# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c37 P8](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0008), [v4 c37 P20](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0020)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Cornelia has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face with jolly brown eyes. Her fair hair is styled in a hard little knob, secured by an elastic band tight under her head rather than held with hat pins. She does not look like the traditional old maid despite her oddities of attire.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)_

## Personality

Miss Cornelia possesses a sharp, bitter tongue alongside a deeply compassionate heart, always stepping in to help gently whenever there is trouble. She harbours a strong disdain for men and Methodists, often expressing sharp opinions about them. Plainspoken and practical, she snubs flowery or high-falutin language from men on principle and accepts unalterable facts without wasting time on useless arguments. She enjoys reading obituary notices as a form of recreation.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c26 P25](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0025), [v4 c28 P0](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0000), [v4 c28 P3](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0003), [v4 c30 P48](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0048)_

## History

Miss Cornelia grew up as an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born. In her youth, she had her pick of suitors but remained unmarried for many years, earning a reputation in Four Winds for her sharp tongue and kind nature. She formed a close friendship with Leslie Moore, standing by her as her best friend and helper through hardship. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, Cornelia recognized a kindred spirit and quickly became a frequent visitor at the Blythe house, engaging in lively verbal sparring matches with her old friend Captain Jim. She later arranged for Owen Ford to board with Leslie and loyally defended Leslie against local gossip. Eventually, Cornelia agreed to marry Marshall Elliott, satisfied at least by the fact that he was a fellow Presbyterian.
